newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - No Swedish interest rate cut on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - No Swedish interest rate cut on Thursday.

text.p: The Swedish central bank, the Riksbank, will leave its key repurchase rate and its lending and deposit rates unchanged at its regular Thursday board meeting, said most analysts in a Reuter poll on Wednesday.
"No, we do not think that they will cut either the repo or the corridor tomorrow," said Ake Gustavsson, economist at Swedbank, based here.
The Riksbank's regular board meeting is scheduled to begin at 0745 GMT on Thursday.
But Gustavsson said "it is possible that they will make a statement. They have not done that since the inflation report on December 17. That could dispel some of the confusion in the market."
Of the eleven economists surveyed, only two believed the Riksbank would cut rates on Thursday.
Several economists instead forecast a cut in the repo rate next Tuesday at its regular tender at 0830 GMT.
Most of the economists did not expect a cut in the lending and deposit rates, which make up the interest rate corridor in which the repo rate moves.
"They usually do not cut the corridor until they need to," one economist said.
The repo rate currently stands at 4.10 percent, the deposit rate at 3.75 percent and the lending rate at 5.25 percent. -- Charlotte Meynert, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1071
